questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Passage: Consider the following reaction sequence in which $\textbf{J}$, $\textbf{K}$, $\textbf{L}$ and $\textbf{M}$ are the major products.

Given:
Atomic mass (in amu): H : $1$, C : $12$, N : $14$, O : $16$, S : $32$, Br : $80$, Ba : $137$

Question: In sulphur estimation by Carius method, the amount of BaSO$_4$ formed from $3.79$ g of $\textbf{M}$ is ____ g.
questions.solution:
Step 1: The starting material is $m$-xylene (1,3-dimethylbenzene). It undergoes Friedel-Crafts acylation with chloroacetyl chloride ($\text{ClCH}_2\text{COCl}$) in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form 2-chloro-1-(2,4-dimethylphenyl)ethanone.

Step 2: The chloro ketone reacts with $\text{NaI}$ (Finkelstein reaction) to form 2-iodo-1-(2,4-dimethylphenyl)ethanone.

Step 3: This iodo compound undergoes Williamson ether synthesis with sodium 3-nitrophenoxide to form compound $\textbf{J}$.
The molecular formula of $\textbf{J}$ is $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{15}\text{NO}_4$.

Step 4: Compound $\textbf{J}$ is reduced by $\text{NaBH}_4$, which converts the ketone group to a secondary alcohol. Subsequent reaction with $\text{PBr}_3$ replaces the hydroxyl group with a bromine atom, yielding compound $\textbf{K}$.
The molecular formula of $\textbf{K}$ is $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{16}\text{BrNO}_3$.
Molar mass of $\textbf{K} = (16 \times 12) + (16 \times 1) + 80 + 14 + (3 \times 16) = 350 \text{ g/mol}$, which matches the given data.

Step 5: Compound $\textbf{K}$ reacts with sodium thiophenoxide ($\text{PhSNa}$) in an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction, replacing the bromide with a phenylthio group ($\text{-SPh}$) to form compound $\textbf{M}$.
The molecular formula of $\textbf{M}$ is $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{16}(\text{SC}_6\text{H}_5)\text{NO}_3 \Rightarrow \text{C}_{22}\text{H}_{21}\text{NO}_3\text{S}$.
Molar mass of $\textbf{M} = 350 - 80 (\text{for Br}) + 109 (\text{for SPh}) = 379 \text{ g/mol}$.

Step 6: Calculate the moles of compound $\textbf{M}$ used in the Carius method.
$\text{Moles of } \textbf{M} = \dfrac{3.79 \text{ g}}{379 \text{ g/mol}} = 0.01 \text{ mol}$.

Step 7: Since each molecule of $\textbf{M}$ contains exactly one sulphur atom, the moles of sulphur present is $0.01 \text{ mol}$. In the Carius method, all sulphur is quantitatively converted to barium sulphate ($\text{BaSO}_4$).
$\text{Moles of BaSO}_4 \text{ formed} = 0.01 \text{ mol}$.

Step 8: Calculate the mass of $\text{BaSO}_4$ formed.
Molar mass of $\text{BaSO}_4 = 137 (\text{Ba}) + 32 (\text{S}) + 4 \times 16 (\text{O}) = 233 \text{ g/mol}$.
$\text{Mass of BaSO}_4 = 0.01 \text{ mol} \times 233 \text{ g/mol} = 2.33 \text{ g}$.

Answer: $2.33$

questions.q: The correct option(s) to distinguish nitrate salts of $M{n}^{2 +}andC{u}^{2 +}$ taken separately is(are)
options: $M{n}^{2 +}$ shows the characteristic green colour in the flame test
Only $C{u}^{2 +}$ shows the formation of precipitate by passing ${H}_{2}S$ in acidic medium
Only $M{n}^{2 +}$ shows the formation of precipitate by passing ${H}_{2}S$ in faintly basic medium
$C{u}^{2 +} / Cu$ has higher reduction potential than $M{n}^{2 +} / Mn$ (measured under similar conditions)
questions.solution:
$( A )$ $C{u}^{+ 2}andM{n}^{+ 2}$ both gives green colour in flame test and cannot distinguished
$( B )$ $C{u}^{+ 2}$ belongs to group-II of cationic radical will gives ppt. of CuS in acidic medium
$( C )$ $C{u}^{+ 2}andM{n}^{+ 2}$ both form ppt. in basic medium
$( D )$ $C{u}^{+ 2} / Cu = + 0.34v\left(SRP\right)$
$M{n}^{+ 2} / Mn = - 0.1 . 18v\left(SRP\right)$

questions.q: The reagent(s) that can selectively precipitate ${S}^{2 -}$ from a mixture of ${S}^{2 -}$ and $S{O}_{4}^{2 -}$ in aqueous solution is (are)
questions.solution:
(A)

$\begin{cases}CuC{l}_{2} & + & S^{2 -} \\ \left(sol^{n}\right) & & \left(sol^{n}\right)\end{cases}\begin{cases}\to & CuS ↓ & + \\ & \left(Blackppt .\right) & \end{cases}\begin{array}{ll}2Cl^{-} \\ \left(Sol^{n}\right)\end{array}$
$\begin{cases}CuC{l}_{2} & + & S{O}_{4}^{2 -} \\ \left(sol^{n}\right) & & \left(sol^{n}\right)\end{cases}\begin{cases}\to & Noppt . \\ & \end{cases}$
(B)

$\begin{cases}BaC{l}_{2} & + & S^{2 -} \\ \left(sol^{n}\right) & & \left(sol^{n}\right)\end{cases}\begin{cases}\to & BaS & + \\ & \left(Noppt .\right) & \end{cases}\begin{array}{ll}2Cl^{-} \\ \left(Sol^{n}\right)\end{array}$
$\begin{cases}BaC{l}_{2} & + & {SO}_{4}^{2 -} \\ \left(sol^{n}\right) & & \left(sol^{n}\right)\end{cases}\begin{cases}\to & BaS{O}_{4} ↓ & + \\ & \left(Whiteppt .\right) & \end{cases}\begin{array}{ll}2Cl^{-} \\ \left(Sol^{n}\right)\end{array}$
(C)

$\begin{cases}Pb{\left(OOCC{H}_{3}\right)}_{2} & + & S^{2 -} \\ \left(sol^{n}\right) & & \left(sol^{n}\right)\end{cases}\begin{cases}\to & PbS ↓ & + \\ & \left(Blackppt .\right) & \end{cases}\begin{array}{ll}2C{H}_{3}COO^{-} \\ \left(Sol^{n}\right)\end{array}$
$\begin{cases}Pb{\left(OOCC{H}_{3}\right)}_{2} & + & {SO}_{4}^{2 -} \\ \left(sol^{n}\right) & & \left(sol^{n}\right)\end{cases}\begin{cases}\to & PbS{O}_{4} ↓ & + \\ & \left(Whiteppt .\right) & \end{cases}\begin{array}{ll}2C{H}_{3}COO^{-} \\ \left(Sol^{n}\right)\end{array}$
(D)

$\begin{cases}N{a}_{2}\left[Fe{\left(CN\right)}_{5}NO\right] & + & S^{2 -} \\ \left(sol^{n}\right) & & \left(sol^{n}\right)\end{cases}\begin{cases}\to & N{a}_{4}\left[Fe{\left(CN\right)}_{5}NOS\right] \\ & ( Purplecoloursolution )\end{cases}$
$\begin{cases}N{a}_{2}\left[Fe{\left(CN\right)}_{5}NO\right] & + & {SO}_{4}^{2 -} \\ \left(sol^{n}\right) & & \left(sol^{n}\right)\end{cases}\begin{cases}\to & Noppt . \\ & \end{cases}$
Note: $\left\begin{array}{ll}PbS{O}_{4}Ksp = 2.5 \times {10}^{- 8} \\ PbSKsp = 3 \times {10}^{- 28}\end{array}\right\}Whicharenotgiveninquestion$
As in question selective precipitation is asked $\text{P}\text{b}\text{S}$ will be precipitate much easier than $PbS{O}_{4}$ though both are insoluble. Hence, answer should be $\text{P}\text{b}{( \text{O}\text{O}\text{C} - \text{C}{H}_{3} )}_{2}$ also along with $\text{C}\text{u}\text{C}{l}_{2}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Upon treatment with ammoniacal ${\text{H}}_{2} \text{S}$, the metal ion that precipitates as a sulphide is
questions.solution:
Among Fe3+, Al3+, Mg2+ and Zn2+, only Zn2+ is precipitated with ammoniacal H2S as ZnS.

The group III metal ions, in presence of NH4OH when H2S is bubbled through filtrate Ni2+, Co2+ and Zn2+ are precipitated as sulphides.

questions.q: Identify the binary mixture(s) that can be separated into individual compounds, by differential extraction as shown in the given scheme.
questions.solution:
(a) Both are soluble in $\mathrm{NaOH}$. Hence, inseparable.

(b) Only benzoic acid $\left(\mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{5} \mathrm{COOH}\right)$ is soluble in $\mathrm{NaOH} and \mathrm{NaHCO}_{3}$, while benzyl alcohol $\left(\mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{5} \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{OH}\right)$ is not. Hence, separable.

(c) Although $\mathrm{NaOH}$ can enable separation between benzyl alcohol $\left(\mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{5} \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{OH}\right)$ and phenol $\left(\mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{5} \mathrm{OH}\right)$ as only the latter is soluble in $\mathrm{NaOH}$. However, in $\mathrm{NaHCO}_{3}$, both are insoluble. Hence, inseparable.

(d) $\alpha$-Phenylacetic acid $\left(\mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{5} \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{COOH}\right)$ is soluble in $\mathrm{NaOH} and \mathrm{NaHCO}_{3}$, while benzyl alcohol $\left(\mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{5} \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{OH}\right)$ is not. Hence, separable.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A solution when diluted with $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ and boiled, it gives a white precipitate. On addition of excess $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl} / \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$, the volume of precipitate decreases leaving behind a white gelatinous precipitate. Identify the precipitate which dissolves in $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH} / \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$.
questions.solution: A solution of $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ ion reacts with water which on boiling give white ppt. of $\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{OH})_2$. This precipitates dissolve in excess of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ in presence of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$ because $\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{OH})_2$ on reaction with $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ in presence of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$ forms tetrammine zinc (II) complex (soluble).
